mars.q: In the command `move()`, what are the round brackets called?
mars.why: The round brackets are a pair of parentheses. Every function call needs them, even when nothing goes inside.

mars.q: When you write `def turn_right():` you ______ a function. (one word)
mars.why: `def` defines the function: it gives a name to a set of actions. Writing `turn_right()` later on calls it.

mars.q: Your program calls `turn_around()` but the function was never defined. Which error does Python show?
mars.why: An undefined function gives NameError: name 'turn_around' is not defined. Python does not know what that name means.

mars.q: Breaking a large problem into smaller, more manageable sub-problems is called ______.
mars.why: Decomposition: each small problem becomes one short helper function, and `main()` calls them in order.

mars.q: Which of these is the function where the program starts?
mars.why: The main function is the starting point. The last two lines of every file call it.

mars.q: Which line correctly begins a function definition?
mars.why: The keyword is `def`, the name is followed by parentheses, and the line ends with a colon before the indented body.

warehouse.q: A loop that repeats a block of code a specific number of times is called a ...
warehouse.why: A for loop with `range(4)` is a definite loop: you know in advance it runs four times.

warehouse.q: The indented lines inside a loop, which run every time the loop repeats, are called ...
warehouse.why: The body of the loop is everything indented under the `for` or `while` line.

warehouse.q: One repetition of a loop is called one ______.
warehouse.why: To iterate is to repeat; each repetition is an iteration.

options: what must be true before a function is called
what is true after a function has finished
warehouse.why: The pre-condition is the starting situation the function expects, e.g. "the robot is on a corner, facing east". The post-condition describes the situation afterwards.

warehouse.q: A loop runs one time too few, so the last square is missed. This mistake is known as ...
warehouse.why: Fence post problem: a fence with 5 rails needs 6 posts. Loops that pair a put with a move often miss the last post.

options: a definite loop - it always runs a fixed number of times
an indefinite loop - it runs as long as a condition is true
ocean.why: A while loop does not count. It checks its condition before every iteration and stops when the condition becomes false.

ocean.q: A test that is either True or False, such as `front_is_clear()`, is called a ______.
ocean.why: A condition. Its value is a boolean: `True` or `False`.

ocean.q: In `if front_is_clear():` ... `else:` ..., when does the `else` block run?
ocean.why: The if-else statement has two paths: the `if` block runs when the condition is true, the `else` block when it is false.

ocean.q: What kind of value does `bottle_present()` give back?
ocean.why: Sensors return a boolean (`True` or `False`), which is why they can be used directly as a condition.

ocean.q: A mistake in a program that makes it behave unexpectedly is called a ______.
ocean.why: A bug. Finding and fixing bugs is called debugging.

ocean.q: An `if` inside the body of a `while` loop means the program has ...
ocean.why: Each block is indented one level deeper than the line that opens it, so the code inside the `if` is two levels in.

console.q: The user types `9` when asked by `input()`. What type of value does the program receive?
console.why: `input()` always gives back a string, even when the user types digits. Use `int()` to convert it.

console.q: `int("9")` ______ the string into a whole number. (one verb)
console.why: It converts (changes) the value from one type to another. `str()` converts the other way.

console.q: Joining strings together with `+`, as in `"hi" + " there"`, is called ...
console.why: Concatenation. The `+` operator adds numbers but concatenates strings.

console.q: What is the type of the result of `7 / 2`?
console.why: Division with `/` always gives a float (`3.5`). Whole-number division uses `//`.

console.q: The naming style `num_students`, lowercase words joined by underscores, is called ______ case.
console.why: Snake case is the Python convention for variable and function names.

console.q: What does the line `total = total + 1` do?
options: works out total + 1, then stores the result back in total
console.why: Assignment: Python first evaluates the right-hand side, then stores the result in the variable on the left. It is not the same as "equals" in maths.
